description:
## Outcome

The CLI and daemon have explicit cross-platform boundaries for shutdown, file access, process launch, and path handling. Windows does not depend on Unix signals, modes, or shell syntax.

## Work

1. Audit production code and package scripts for Unix-only permissions, signals, executable bits, path separators, quoting, and shell commands.
2. Add a shutdown source for Windows console and service-manager stop events. Keep the Unix signal adapter for Unix.
3. Route file privacy through the platform access-control capability.
4. Use argument-vector process launch and platform launchers. Do not build command strings with user paths.
5. Add tests for drive paths, UNC-like invalid cases, spaces, non-ASCII profiles, reserved names, and long paths where supported.
6. Document any supported Windows Terminal requirement and old Console Host non-goal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Windows shutdown does not call the Unix `SIGTERM` implementation.
- [ ] No supported Windows path passes through a POSIX shell.
- [ ] Token and state privacy use Windows access control, not ignored Unix modes.
- [ ] Launchers preserve arguments that contain spaces and Unicode.
- [ ] The audit has no unexplained Unix-only production operation.
- [ ] Windows-specific tests run on a native Windows runner.

## Tests

Add platform capability tests and native Windows integration checks. Run the normal quality, coverage, and docs commands on Unix and the selected checks on Windows.

## Non-goals

Do not register a Windows service or support old Windows Console Host graphics in this task.
title: Make file, signal, and shell boundaries portable to Windows
